text:
zoe.sales: Hi team — attending TechSummit next week. Questions: conference registration, a small client dinner, and two client gifts (branded notebook + local artisanal bottle). Which of these are reimbursable and any limits?

cara.peopleops: Welcome to the fun world of travel spend :) Conference registration is reimbursable as Training/Conference if it's business-related and you attach agenda and proof of attendance. Client dinners are entertainment and reimbursable but need attendee names and business purpose. Gifts: company policy caps small gifts at $50 per recipient without additional approvals. Anything > $50 needs manager + compliance sign-off.

matt.finance: Finance notes: attach invoices/receipts and list recipients for client meals/gifts. Code entries: Conference fee -> Travel > Conference. Client dinner -> Travel > Meals/Entertainment. Gifts -> Sales > Client Gifts. If corporate card used, tag transaction as CORPORATE; if personal, submit reimbursement with receipts.

zoe.sales: The artisanal bottle is ~ $65. I guess that's > $50. What does approval look like and are bottles allowed (alcohol)?

compliance-bot: Policy reminder: Alcoholic beverages can be given as client gifts in most jurisdictions but check local anti-bribery rules. Gifts that could influence procurement decisions require higher scrutiny. Gifts must be reasonable, infrequent, and transparent.

cara.peopleops: Practically: for the $65 bottle, include a short justification (client relationship building, non-procurement contact, not part of a selection process) and tag your manager. Compliance will review and approve/decline. If declined, consider substituting a non-alcoholic gift under $50.

matt.finance: Also note tax/treatments: gifts to clients may be nondeductible in some jurisdictions above a threshold. We'll annotate the expense for tax. If the gift is shipped internationally, customs/duty may apply and that's generally not reimbursable without prior approval.

zoe.sales: For the client dinner, do I need itemized receipts and attendee list? We had a table of 4, client picked up half the tab, I covered \u0024120 on company card.

cara.peopleops: Yes please: itemized restaurant receipt showing line items, and a short attendee list (name + company) and business purpose (e.g., "post-demo follow-up; discussed integration timeline"). If the client paid part, attach their receipt or a note that client covered X. Manager approval required for entertainment spend.

matt.finance: If the restaurant receipt isn't itemized and only shows a total, include a quick note splitting food vs alcohol if relevant. For split bills where client paid part, indicate the net company expense. For amounts > \u0024100 for entertainment, a manager approver is mandatory.

zoe.sales: One more nuance  the conference registration included optional social events with ticketed dinners. Can I expense the attendee dinner ticket?

cara.peopleops: Ticketed conference social events that are part of the conference experience are generally reimbursable if business-related. However, if the social event is purely personal (guest + spouse) or an expensive gala, check limits and get pre-approval.

matt.finance: If the conference gives an invoice showing the extra social event line, treat that like a conference fee (Travel > Conference). If it's charged separately on the card, attach the event description so we can justify it.

expense-bot: Reminder: please include cost_center and project_code in the expense. Missing approver will cause the claim to be routed back.

zoe.sales: If compliance needs to sign off on the \u002465 bottle, how long does that take? I need to buy before the show.

compliance-bot: Typical turnaround for gift approval is 1-3 business days depending on complexity. For alcohol or gifts > $50, provide recipient role, relationship to procurement decisions, and a brief justification to speed review.

zoe.sales: Got it. Any suggestions to avoid borderline approvals?

cara.peopleops: Two options: pick non-alcoholic gifts under \u002450 (branded notebooks, local snacks), or request a pre-approved "swag pack" from Marketing which is pre-cleared for client gifting. If urgent, ask manager to approve and tag Compliance with a short note.

matt.finance: Also: keep receipts clean, avoid cash payments for gifts if possible (paper trail matters). For international gifts, consider buying locally at destination to avoid shipping/customs and document vendor VAT if reclaimable.

zoe.sales: Great. Could you paste a sample expense note I can use?

matt.finance: Sure — paste this and edit amounts/dates:
```
TechSummit 2026 conference (attendance and client meetings):
- Conference registration: $300 (invoice attached; agenda/proof of attendance attached)
- Client dinner 2026-09-14: $120 (Company covered). Attendees: Zoe Smith (Redwood), John Doe (ACME Corp), Priya Patel (ACME Corp), Tim Lee (Redwood). Business purpose: post-demo follow-up on integration timeline. Itemized receipt attached. Manager @laura.sales approved 2026-09-10.
- Client gift: Artisanal bottle $65 (recipient: John Doe, ACME Corp). Justification: relationship building post-demo; not part of procurement evaluation. Manager @laura.sales and Compliance pre-approved 2026-09-10 (approval thread attached). Code: Sales > Client Gifts; Cost_center: SALES-US; Project_code: PROJ-789.
```

zoe.sales: Perfect, will request compliance approval now and upload the docs once approved. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
